package_info.package_manager: N/A (delivered via phishing, not a public package repository)
package_info.why_malicious: MrAnon Stealer is a multi-stage info-stealer malware distributed via phishing emails. It uses a combination of .NET, PowerShell, and Python (cx-Freeze packed) payloads to steal credentials, browser sessions, cryptocurrency wallets, and sensitive files, then exfiltrates the data to public file-sharing sites and the attacker's Telegram channel.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Downloader link hidden in PDF stream object, which, when clicked, downloads a .NET executable (adobe.exe) from anonbin[.]ir.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user opens the PDF and clicks the link, the code initiates a download of a .NET executable from a remote server, enabling the next stage of infection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: PDFs with hidden downloader links are a common phishing technique to deliver malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate PDFs should not contain hidden links that download executables.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Corporate PDFs may contain links, but not to executables from untrusted domains.
key_indicators: Downloader link hidden in PDF stream

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The .NET executable uses ScriptRunner.dll to extract Scripts.zip, then unpacks and executes down2.ps1 via PowerShell.exe.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon execution, the .NET binary unpacks an embedded PowerShell script and launches it, enabling further payload delivery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Dropping and executing PowerShell scripts from executables is a common malware tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate installers do not silently unpack and execute PowerShell scripts from embedded resources.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: PowerShell script loads a Windows Form, fetches a zip payload from anonbin[.]ir, decompresses it, and executes python.exe. Displays a fake error window ('File Not Supported', 'Not Run: python.exe') to mislead the user.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the script downloads a zip archive from a remote server, extracts and executes a malicious binary, and displays a deceptive error message to hide successful execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing binaries from the internet is highly suspicious, especially when combined with user deception.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts should not fetch and execute remote binaries or mislead users with fake error messages.
key_indicators: Fake error message to hide activity

execution_context.file_location: python.exe (from extracted zip, not a legitimate Python interpreter)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: python.exe (cx-Freeze packed) searches for \lib\library.zip and loads cstgversion__main__.pyc using PyObject_CallObject.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the binary loads a malicious Python module from a bundled zip archive, enabling execution of the info-stealer payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Non-standard Python executables loading code from bundled archives is a common malware packing technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Python applications do not obfuscate their main logic in this way.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malware terminates processes (e.g., ArmoryQt.exe, chrome.exe, Discord.exe, etc.), captures screenshot, collects browser data, wallet data, files with sensitive extensions, compresses data, uploads to gofile[.]io, and sends download link/system info to Telegram via bot token.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code kills selected processes, steals credentials and files, exfiltrates data to a public file-sharing site, and notifies the attacker via Telegram.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Mass data theft, process termination, and exfiltration to public and attacker-controlled channels are hallmarks of info-stealer malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not kill unrelated processes, steal sensitive data, or exfiltrate it to unknown servers.

attack_chain.action: User receives phishing email with malicious PDF attachment.
attack_chain.leads_to: User opens PDF and clicks downloader link.

attack_chain.action: Downloader link in PDF fetches .NET executable (adobe.exe) from remote server.
.NET executable unpacks and runs PowerShell script (down2.ps1).
PowerShell script downloads and extracts zip payload, executes python.exe, and displays fake error message.
python.exe loads and executes malicious Python code from library.zip.
Malicious Python code steals data, exfiltrates to gofile[.]io, and sends notification to attacker's Telegram.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen data and system info.

behavioral_signatures: PDF attachments with hidden downloader links
Execution of .NET binaries that unpack and run PowerShell scripts
PowerShell scripts downloading and executing remote binaries
Fake error dialogs masking malware execution
cx-Freeze packed Python executables loading .pyc from library.zip
Process termination of browsers, wallets, and security tools
Exfiltration to public file-sharing sites and Telegram bots
file_indicators: adobe.exe in temp or downloads directory
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for emails with PDF attachments containing hidden downloader links. Detect execution of .NET binaries that unpack and run PowerShell scripts, especially those that download further payloads from suspicious domains. Flag PowerShell scripts that download and execute binaries, display fake error dialogs, or drop non-standard python.exe files. Look for cx-Freeze packed Python executables loading .pyc files from library.zip. Alert on process termination of browsers, wallets, and security tools, as well as bulk file compression and uploads to public file-sharing sites or Telegram bots.
